subject: Common factor model with SNPs - negative variances warning

messages.author: 80171ab3d7adb6ab
messages.subject: Common factor model with SNPs - negative variances warning
parts:
To all, 

Again, thanks for all your help.  

Q1. Running a common factor model- 3 traits - 1 binary - with SNPS, generated, under fail, 0s, but under warning, the message:

lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative

You mentioned this warning in the wiki.  How would I correct my model or data so as to avoid the negative variances? 

Best, 

Dan

messages.author: c78bfd9857351762
messages.subject: Re: Common factor model with SNPs - negative variances warning
parts:
More information about my problem.

I ran the common factor (without SNPs) model.
   lhs op     rhs Unstandardized_Estimate Unstandardized_SE Standardized_Est Standardized_SE      p_value
1      F1 =~ A              0.41204732       0.077693144        1.4123002      0.26629477 1.135893e-07
2      F1 =~   B              0.10426350       0.020436219        0.3836125      0.07519016 3.362646e-07
3      F1 =~ C             0.05787445       0.012748455        0.2361044      0.05200854 5.632830e-06
5 A ~~ A            -0.08466133       0.063902196       -0.9945919      0.75071596 1.852183e-01
6   B ~~   B              0.06300098       0.005014037        0.8528414      0.06787479 3.292029e-36
7 C ~~ C              0.05673550       0.004982201        0.9442547      0.08291928 4.818795e-30

If I understand it, this is the Heywood case.  The standardardized_Est for trait A > 1 would for give me negative variances, and standardized variance <1. 
In part2, common factor (without SNPs), you recommend using a model to impose a constraint to keep the residual variance above 0. Is there a way to incorporate that same constraint into the common factor with SNPs model?

Best, 

Dan

messages.author: c78bfd9857351762
messages.subject: Re: Common factor model with SNPs - negative variances warning
parts:
Reviewing the wiki, I attempted to constrain variance of trait to > 0, as follows:

commonfactor.model<-"F1=~ NA*A + B+ C
F1 ~ SNP
F1~~1*F1"
pfactor_10R <- userGWAS(covstruc = LDSCoutput, SNPs = p_sumstats_10, estimation = "DWLS", model = commonfactor.model, printwarn = TRUE, sub="F1~SNP")

Where A is the trait with the negative variance.  

Unfortunately, my model specification did not work.

Again, I would appreciate any help you can give me in this.

Best, 
Dan
